messages.subject: Getting soil temp at depth using micro_terra
messages.subject_clean: Getting soil temp at depth using micro_terra
messages.body_plain:
Hi Mike,

I was trying to get hourly soil temps at specific depths for 20 years for 20k+ sites using micro_terra. However, this resulted in being very slow and hard to run in parallel as the function read .nc files for each location. If scenario=2 or 4, the function would even read .nc files for both current and future climates!

Is there any possible solution to this? Can I modify the function and let it run through multiple locations after a one-time data reading? Do I really need to read in .nc files for current climates when running for future climates?

Your help would be most appreciated!

I used NicheMapR 3.2.1, R version 4.1.2, and Ubuntu 22.04.1

Here is the code I used:

cal.micro<-function(lon,lat,scenario){
  micro<-try(micro_terra(
    #Type in parameters that are not default
    scenario=scenario,
    terra_source="/home/2/TerraClim/data",
    loc=c(lon,lat),
    ystart=1996,
    yfinish=2015,
    timeinterval=365,
    DEP=c(0,3,6,12,18,24,30,40,69,200)
  ))
  micro[c(1:2)]
}

Best,

Liang

Hi Liang,

You would indeed need to come up with your own scripts, with one that reads everything from terraclimate first in parallel, constructs the climate scenarios if needed, and then saves them somewhere (possibly easiest as RData objects), and then a second one that runs the microclimate calculations. The climate change scenarios are imposed on current climates hence the need to query both.

All the best,
Mike

Hi all,

I am managing to run the ectotherm model with micro_era5, but would like to change the scenario to identify changes in my organisms activity. When I do change this, I receive the following error -

error: maxshades must be a vector with a length equal to the number of days simulated
error: minshades must be a vector with a length equal to the number of days simulated

I have noticed others with the same error on this forum, but they are usually changing parameters in the microclimate model which I am not. The only thing I change is the scenario (scenario = 2), everything else is set to default. Then when the ectotherm model is run the above errors occur.
I have looked the number of days min/max are calculated for, with both being the same length as days simulated. I have specified minshades <- micro$minshade and
maxshades <- micro$maxshade in the ectotherm model which returns the same error. I have run the default micro_ncep which returns results with the ectotherm model, but with the scenario change it returns the same error.

Does anyone have any suggestions as to what I'm overlooking here?

Thank you,

Shane

messages.subject: NicheMapR v3.3.1 released
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I just put out a new release of NicheMapR <https://github.com/mrke/NicheMapR/releases/tag/v3.3.1> - the changes are all explained in the notes for the release. Of the major additions, the leaf temperature aspects are part of a paper that should come out in the next few months, the torpor model will also be part of a paper that's a fair way through the review process and the the snakey DEB things are part of a project I'm working on at the moment.

I updated the help on the NicheMapR website to include a couple of new vignettes too, one on leaf temperature calculations <https://mrke.github.io/NicheMapR/inst/doc/leaf-temperature-tutorial> and another on the Soil Plant Atmosphere Continuum (SPAC) model <https://mrke.github.io/NicheMapR/inst/doc/Campbell_SPAC_infiltration> used in the microclimate model to compute soil moisture as a function of a transpiring plant.

All the best,
Mike

#run microclimate model
micro<-try(micro_era5(#Type in parameters that are not default

Best,
Dave

Hi Zhong-wen,

OK so it seems the integrator isn't able to balance the energy/mass budget of the soil with those settings with the default error tolerance (i.e., how close to zero the energy/mass balance gets to when it's integrating). It does need a certain spacing of soil nodes to work properly, so avoiding big departures from the default settings is a good idea. ERR=2 is still pretty good so if that works, it might be fine.

But a better solution would be to do two simulations that give you all the depths you need. It may be that having no nodes between 69cm and 2m is the problem, so you could try removing one shallow node, say 12 cm, and add 150cm, and see if that works. Plot the results, esp. the near soil temps and the soil moisture and snow, to see how much of a difference it's making to the calculations, compared to upping the ERR value. I'd avoid going higher than 2.5.

You could add a trycatch so that if it hits trouble it increases ERR until a threshold of 2.5. Below is an example of some code I wrote for doing lots of sites and catching errors, which you could adapt to your situation (note it also checks if there's available future climate, which isn't always the case, and saves the DEM data for the site if it hasn't been done before, since that is always the same and it takes time if you're having to rerun sites):

  for(jj in 2000:2000){
    ystart <- jj
    yfinish <- ystart
    scenario <- 2

    nyears <- yfinish - ystart + 1

    microdir <- paste0(outdir, 'micro/', ystart, '_', scenario)
    if(!dir.exists(microdir)){
      dir.create(microdir)
    }

    # micro parameters
    REFL <- 0.2
    Usrhyt <- 0.8

    for(ii in 1:nrow(longlats2)){
      loc <- c(longlats2$lng[ii], longlats2$lat[ii])
      citynum <- longlats2$num[ii]
      if(!file.exists(paste0(microdir, '/micro_', citynum, '.Rda'))){
        # set initial conditions

        if(!file.exists(paste0(outdir, 'dem/dem_', citynum , '.Rda'))){
          dem <- NULL
          attempt <- 0
          while( is.null(dem) && attempt <= 30 ) {
            attempt <- attempt + 1
            try(
              dem <- microclima::get_dem(lat = loc[2], long = loc[1], resolution = 30, xdims = 100, ydims = 100) # mercator equal area projection
            )
            elevera5 <- microclima::get_dem(r = NA, lat = loc[2], long = loc[1], resolution = 10000, xdims = 10, ydims = 10)
            lar <- round(loc[2] * 4, 0)/4
            lor <- round(loc[1] * 4, 0)/4
            e <- extent(lor - 0.875, lor + 0.875, lar - 0.875, lar + 0.875)
            e5d <- projectRaster(elevera5, crs = sf::st_crs(4326)$wkt)
            rte <- raster(e)
            res(rte) <- 0.25
            e5d <- resample(e5d, rte)
            xy <- data.frame(x = loc[1], y = loc[2])
            weather.elev <- raster::extract(e5d, xy)
          }
          save(dem, file = paste0(outdir, 'dem/dem_', citynum , '.Rda'))
          save(weather.elev, file = paste0(outdir, 'dem/weather.elev_', citynum , '.Rda'))
          temploc <- tempdir()
        }

        load(paste0(outdir, 'dem/dem_', citynum , '.Rda'))
        load(paste0(outdir, 'dem/weather.elev_', citynum , '.Rda'))

        # run microclimate model
        ERR <- 1.5
        continue <- TRUE
        if(scenario != 0){
          terra_source = "http://thredds.northwestknowledge.net:8080/thredds/dodsC/TERRACLIMATE_ALL/data"
          nyears <- yfinish - ystart + 1
          if(yfinish > 2015){
            ystart_terra <- 2015 - nyears + 1
            yfinish_terra <- 2015
            message(paste0("terraclimate climate change scenarios are for 1985 to 2015 - using ", ystart, "-", yfinish), '\n')
          }else{
            ystart_terra <- ystart
            yfinish_terra <- yfinish
          }
          tryCatch(                       # Applying tryCatch

            expr = {                      # Specifying expression
              terra <- as.data.frame(get_terra(x = loc, ystart = ystart_terra, yfinish = yfinish_terra, source = terra_source))
              message("Everything was fine.")
            },

            error = function(e){          # Specifying error message
              message("There was an error message.")
            },

            warning = function(w){        # Specifying warning message
              message("There was a warning message.")
              continue <<-FALSE
            },

            finally = {                   # Specifying final message
              message("tryCatch is finished.")
            }
          )
        }
        if (continue) {
          micro <- micro_era5_local(terra_source = terra_source, dem = dem, fail = 5, ERR = ERR, slope = 0, loc = loc, dstart = paste0('01/01/', ystart-1), dfinish = paste0('31/12/', yfinish), Usrhyt = Usrhyt, REFL = REFL, spatial = '/ERA5/time', scenario = scenario, weather.elev = weather.elev, runshade = 0)
          gc()
          while(min(micro$metout[,1])==0 & ERR <= 3){
            cat("model crashed, trying a higher error tolerance \n")
            ERR <- ERR + 0.25
            micro <- micro_era5_local(terra_source = terra_source, dem = dem, fail = 5, ERR = ERR, slope = 0, loc = loc, dstart = paste0('01/01/', ystart-1), dfinish = paste0('31/12/', yfinish), Usrhyt = Usrhyt, REFL = REFL, spatial = '/ERA5/time', scenario = scenario, weather.elev = weather.elev, runshade = 0)
            gc()
          }
          if(min(micro$metout[,1])>0){
            dni <- micro$microclima.out$hourlydata$rad_dni
            dif <- micro$microclima.out$hourlydata$rad_dif
            diffuse_frac <- dif / (dif + dni)
            diffuse_frac[is.na <http://is.na>(micro$diffuse_frac)] <- 1
            #micro <- list(metout = micro$metout, soil = micro$soil, microclima.out = micro$microclima.out, diffuse_frac = diffuse_frac, REFL = micro$REFL, elev = micro$elev)
            micro <- list(metout = micro$metout, soil = micro$soil, diffuse_frac = diffuse_frac, REFL = micro$REFL, elev = micro$elev)
            save(micro, file = paste0(microdir, '/micro_', citynum, '.Rda'))
          }
          temploc <- tempdir()
          #unlink(temploc, recursive = TRUE)
          file.remove(list.files(temploc, include.dirs = TRUE, full.names = TRUE))
        }
      }
    }
  }

All the best,
Mike

Hi Shane,

Thanks for bringing this to my attention. I was surprised you were facing this error about your request having too many fields: for years the limit for ERA5 has been 120,000 fields, and yet your error says the limit is 60,000. A 120,000 for ERA5 hourly single levels is still what the ECMWF documentation Confluence says (see Table 2 here <https://confluence.ecmwf.int/display/CKB/Climate+Data+Store+%28CDS%29+documentation#heading-DatahostedontheCDSMARSinternal>).

But after some digging, I see that in a blog post, the limit for ERA5 just changed from 120,000 to 60,000 in early April, albeit this change should only be temporary:
https://forum.ecmwf.int/t/a-new-cds-soon-to-be-launched-expect-some-disruptions/1607

As for why the number of fields (105120) may have remained the same even though you shrank the spatial extent: given the large grid cell size of ERA5 (0.25 x 0.25), and the rounding of grid coordinates that request_era5() does under the hood, you sometimes need to decrease the extent considerably in order to change the number of fields. But, it's changing the temporal duration that really does any good in changing # of fields: 12 ERA5 variables x 8,760 hourly timesteps = many fields that stack up over time.

So the request you outline above should work in its entirety, but for the time being you'll need to be flexible with the temporary lower field limit. But regardless, as we suggest in our mcera5 paper <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/2041-210X.13877>, and also stated in that blog post, the CDS requests will indeed be much more efficient if you request a shorter temporal duration, as Shane did here, and then combine the netCDF files together. Seeing this (albeit temporary) lower limit of 60,000, I might change the combine = TRUE feature in `request_era5()` so that it's easier to combine months rather than just years...will work on this soon!

Cheers,
Dave
